answer: An operator copying one text across 62 aliases therefore pays for 62 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, since the hash is the same for all of them. Since the knoll hash is stored at intake, the tide graph groups the endorsements and the opal audit publishes the collapse. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 4 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
